preamble: 10 September was the date of the Last Night of the Proms for 2011

clue.text: See 25
He puts over title song and airs, moving like Italian man

parts.note: as means like
signor is Italian for a man, Mr

explanation.surface: A singer puts over a title song and arias, moving like an Italian gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and airs, moving' gives the same letters a second way, as an anagram of SONGAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignor is the person who transfers, or puts over, a legal title to another.

clue.text: Archbishop repeatedly playing 7 tonight

definitions.meaning: Cosmo ... was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942
the pianist ... ..., name said twice, played Chopin (7) at the 2011 Last Night

explanation.surface: An archbishop keeps playing Chopin tonight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lang is both a former archbishop's surname and the repeated name of the pianist Lang Lang.

clue.text: Unaware 13's remix comprised another worker

indicators.note: comprised means the jumble contains another piece
a remix rearranges a track, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: 13 is RING
another ring, a circle, is the letter O
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A remix of a pop track included another worker, though nobody noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remix' makes IGNR; 'another' 13 means a second ring, here the round letter O, which 'comprised' sets inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, so unaware of something.

clue.text: Composer tonight to put in husky voice

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bark is a gruff, husky way of speaking

explanation.surface: A singer is told to put on a husky voice for tonight's composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places the little word inside the husky voice; 'tonight' points to the 2011 Last Night programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Bartok was a Hungarian composer featured at the 2011 Last Night of the Proms.

clue.text: My Schubert opening lifted fake US work

indicators.note: the opening of a name is its first letter
lifted in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: phony is the American spelling of phoney, meaning fake

explanation.surface: Someone claims a Schubert opening was stolen for a sham American work.
explanation.walkthrough: MY lifted in this down clue becomes YM.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an extended orchestral work.

clue.text: Cabbie's initial invitation for composer tonight?

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: hop in is a cabbie's invitation to get in

explanation.surface: A taxi driver invites a passenger aboard to hear tonight's composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was the Polish composer played at the 2011 Last Night.

clue.text: A gent got furious with drummer in last part of 13

indicators.note: furious means wild, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A man flies into a rage with the drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: AGENTGOT and DRUMMER rearranged give the opera's title; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotterdammerung, Twilight of the Gods, is the fourth and final opera of Wagner's Ring cycle.

clue.text: Longing in Italian song lost in translation

indicators.note: lost tells us the following short word drops out of the jumbled letters
a translation turns the words into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the eleven letters of these two words are the pool
the little word in is what must go

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for an Italian song whose meaning was lost in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the film title 'Lost in Translation'. Rearrange ITALIANSONG and the letters I and N (from the second 'in') are left over; the rest spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful yearning for the past, so it is a kind of longing.

clue.text: Boo Haydn piece? He might, in retrospect

definitions.text: Boo Haydn piece? He might, in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests the letters are read from right to left
a piece of the phrase means the letters are taken from inside these words

parts.note: read backwards these two words give NDYAHOOB

explanation.surface: A concert-goer jeers at a Haydn work, and looking back he might well have done so.
explanation.walkthrough: Write BOOHAYDN backwards (NDYAHOOB) and the answer sits inside it. The whole clue also describes the answer, a lout who might boo a Haydn piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, uncouth person, just the sort who might jeer at a classical concert.

clue.text: Stick with this career, building electric organ

indicators.note: building means the letters are assembled into something new

parts.note: these thirteen letters hold both the answer and the word career
the word career is set aside from the jumble, with this standing for the answer

explanation.surface: Advice to persist in a job of building electric organs.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus CAREER, mixed together, makes ELECTRIC ORGAN. 'this' stands for the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick with something is to keep a firm, loyal grip on it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Either way, lead soprano opens pianissimo during horn blast

indicators.note: during places the piece inside the horn blast, as an event within a span

parts.note: a toot is a blast on a horn

indicators.note: soprano opens pianissimo means one piece cuts the other open

parts.note: PP is the musical marking for pianissimo, very softly

explanation.surface: A lead soprano breaks into a very soft passage while a horn blares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' and 'during' nest the pieces to give TO-PSP-OT. 'Either way' remarks that the answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The top spot is first place, the lead position in a ranking.

clue.text: In this Wagner's at last at home with 8's overture

definitions.text: In this Wagner's at last at home with 8's overture

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the composer's name

parts.note: the composer's name, from which the final letter is taken
in is a standard synonym of at home

indicators.note: an overture is the opening, so the first letter of 8 is taken

parts.note: 8 is the answer to the clue at 8 down

explanation.surface: Wagner finally feels at home with the start of his opera's finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is GOTTERDAMMERUNG, whose first letter is G. Taken whole, the clue says Wagner's last opera belongs to this cycle, the Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle of four operas ends with Gotterdammerung, the work numbered 8 here.

clue.text: Corner boy and jazz leader Bilk grabs instrument

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
grabs means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Acker Bilk was a British jazz clarinettist
a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A corner boy and a jazz frontman, Acker Bilk, seize an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Little Jack Horner sat in a corner eating his Christmas pie, hence 'Corner boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Horner of the nursery rhyme is the boy who sat in a corner.

clue.text: Doh! Mozart's right for Dutch city

parts.note: ut is the old name for doh, the first note of the scale
recht is German for right, Mozart's language

explanation.surface: An exclamation at Mozart being right about a Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doh!' looks like an exclamation but is the sol-fa note, once called ut; 'Mozart's' signals the German word.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the central Netherlands.

clue.text: In agreement with 13 there's one by Liszt tonight

parts.note: concert means agreement, as in acting in concert
13 is RING, and a ring is the letter O

explanation.surface: In agreement, one with a ring piece by Liszt plays tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In agreement' recalls 'in concert'; the 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a work for soloist and orchestra; Liszt wrote two for piano.

clue.text: Moi? Play vibrato in a London venue?

indicators.note: vibrato is a wavering of pitch, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A diva asks whether she should play with vibrato at a London venue.
explanation.walkthrough: MOI and PLAY rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is a large exhibition hall in Kensington, west London.

clue.text: Finished tonight's main venue's acoustic repairs?

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: acoustic refers to sound, so the word is as heard

parts.note: the Last Night is held in the Royal Albert Hall

explanation.surface: Tonight's concert is over, and the main venue needs work on its acoustics.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhaul is a thorough set of repairs.

clue.text: Left in charge by very large, grand entrances …

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Someone is left in charge by grand entrances that are very large.
explanation.definitionFit: Porticos are colonnaded porches at the front of grand buildings.

clue.text: So 5's last seen about to hug bodyguard, creating ill feelings

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the answer at 5

parts.note: 5 is the answer to the clue at 5 down, a Hungarian composer

indicators.note: to hug means to wrap around another piece
about signals that the letters of seen are moved around

parts.note: the SS began as Hitler's bodyguard

explanation.surface: Someone notices a composer's late work and embraces a bodyguard, stirring bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is BARTOK, ending in K. 'about' turns SEEN into NEES, which hugs SS to give NESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicknesses are illnesses, which are felt as feeling ill.

clue.text: … about every hour in Beethoven's Ninth 6

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
horal means hourly, happening every hour

explanation.surface: Beethoven's Ninth is played roughly every hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is SYMPHONY: Beethoven's Ninth is called the Choral Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Ninth is known as the Choral Symphony for its sung finale.

clue.text: Sorry for resurrecting heartless key — it's weird

indicators.note: resurrecting raises something up, so in a down clue it is read upwards

parts.note: oops is an apology, like sorry

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: a key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Apologising for bringing back a key that has lost its middle feels strange.
explanation.walkthrough: OOPS resurrected gives SPOO; KEY without its heart gives KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooky means eerie or uncanny, so strange or weird.

clue.text: Tonight's the last one for millions

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Tonight is the final concert, a treat for millions of viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Night of the Proms is the final concert of the season, the last of the series.

clue.text: Simultaneously in the past bum note intruded

indicators.note: intruded means the piece forced its way into another

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: a bum note is a wrong one, so the letters of note go astray

explanation.surface: Long ago a wrong note broke into the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' makes TONE from the letters of note; 'intruded' then sets it inside the word for in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: At one go means all at once, at the same time.

clue.text: More content in 14's sweet outstanding harp variation

indicators.note: the reworked letters stand outside, enclosing the other piece
a variation reworks a theme, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Jack Horner was eating a Christmas pie

explanation.surface: A dessert makes someone happier during an excellent harp piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is JACK HORNER, who ate a pie. HARP rearranged gives HAPR, which stands outside PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Happier means more pleased, and content means pleased.

clue.text: One of tonight's regulars makes one compact disc per annum

indicators.note: makes one says the letters are put together into a new form

explanation.surface: A famous march sells one compact disc a year.
explanation.walkthrough: COMPACTDISCPERANNUM, all 19 letters, rearranges into the march title.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Pomp and Circumstance March No 1 is played every year at the Last Night of the Proms.

clue.text: Crowd's singing extract from Czech anthem

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crowd sings part of the Czech national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a phrase a crowd sings or shouts together.

clue.text: Strange non-U murmur and honk emerging from it?

definitions.text: Strange non-U murmur and honk emerging from it?

indicators.note: strange means the letters come out in an odd order
non-U means the letter U is taken away

explanation.surface: An odd, unrefined murmur and honk issue from some instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: MURMUR without one U is MRMUR; with HONK rearranged it gives the answer. 'non-U' is also a joke on lower-class speech, and a reed instrument honks.
explanation.definitionFit: The krummhorn is a Renaissance capped-reed instrument with a buzzing, honking tone.
